title: Satori business app stand-in model
description: For a demo only: writes a stand-in document type, its schema and page providers over it into a business app package, in a model component of its own that the manifest lists, and describes the type in content-model.json beside the bundle.

package.description: The app definition package, as a path from the workspace root, such as business-apps/packages/acme-contracts.

type.description: The document type: a name of letters, digits, '_' and '-', not one of Nuxeo's own, such as Contract. It extends Document, with the common and dublincore schemas and its own.

properties.description: Writes the type: its properties, separated by commas, each <name>, <name>:<type> or <name>=<value>|<value>. A type is string (the default), long, double, boolean or date, or a list of one but boolean, such as string[]. Values make a string take only those, such as status=Draft|Active.

schema.description: With properties: the schema's name. Defaults to the type's name in lower case.

prefix.description: With properties: the prefix its properties are written with, as in contract:number. Defaults to the schema's name.

pageProvider.description: Writes a page provider over the type, with this name, which a queue or a home names. It reads the repository, or the search index when aggregates are given.

where.description: With pageProvider: an NXQL condition the records must meet besides their type, such as contract:status = 'Active'. A ? is a parameter, which a queue has no record to fill.

sort.description: With pageProvider: its sort, <prefix>:<name> for ascending or <prefix>:<name>:desc. Defaults to dc:modified:desc.

pageSize.description: With pageProvider: records per page, 1 to 100. Defaults to 50.

aggregates.description: With pageProvider: properties of the type, <prefix>:<name> separated by commas, that a queue's facets or a home's figures group the records by. The page provider then reads the search index, which alone answers aggregates, with a terms aggregate <prefix>_<name>_agg for each, and the type gets a search document, <Type>Search. Not with a ? in where: a queue has no record to fill it.

force.description: Write the type's schema again from properties, or the page provider again, when the package has it already.
